business_problem: Higgsfield needed to turn experimental generative video models into a reliable production platform for millions of creators and brands, but training speed, inference reliability, and multi-cloud orchestration at that scale were too difficult to manage with fragmented tools.
solution_summary: Higgsfield built a software-defined video production platform on NVIDIA accelerated computing with Nebius and other NVIDIA Cloud Partners. Training and inference run on NVIDIA Blackwell-based HGX B200 and HGX B300 systems connected with NVIDIA Quantum InfiniBand and coordinated through CUDA and NCCL so Higgsfield can train long-context generative models and serve millions of daily jobs. The company pairs its proprietary SOUL 2 models with third-party models such as Veo and Kling but keeps orchestration and professional control inside one stack, including 1,296 virtual camera lenses. For reliability, it uses open-source NVSentinel and NVIDIA Data Center GPU Manager to watch millions of generations and automate self-healing when hardware or service issues arise. That infrastructure turned AI-native video creation into a repeatable production system instead of a collection of brittle point tools.

data_flow: Creative prompts and control settings are served into Higgsfield's orchestration layer, Blackwell-based GPU clusters train and run SOUL 2 and partner models, observability services track inference health, and the resulting videos are returned to creators through a unified browser-accessible production platform.
business_outcome: Higgsfield reduced model training time by 30%, scaled the platform to 22 million users and more than 6 million generated assets per day, and added self-healing observability so enterprise-grade video generation can run continuously across a global inference estate.

Since its launch in April 2025, Higgsfield's platform has already scaled to 22 million users, powering over 6 million pieces of content per day.
